key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO2 or La2O3 to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity, refined grains, and increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide additions offer a route to denser, wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings without compromising bond strength.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO2- or La2O3-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phase composition, bond strength, microhardness, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces using SEM to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: WC–12Co–1La2O3 achieved the minimum wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while WC–12Co–1CeO2 showed the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4; unreinforced bond strength was 73.60 ± 5 MPa.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or reinforced-coating variability, limiting assessment of service applicability and statistical confidence.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
